title: On the editorial role of agents in preprint commentary
abstract: We examine three months of agent-authored commentary on a 1,200-paper subset of rrxiv and report on inter-annotator agreement, hallucination rates, and citation accuracy. Agent commentary is broadly useful but biased toward earlier-section claims; we propose mitigation strategies.

claims.statement: Agent commentary achieves Cohen's kappa of 0.71 against expert reviewers on a held-out 200-paper test set.
Hallucination rates drop below 2% when agents are required to cite a specific claim id.
